A1.justification: Both PDFs describe AgentRefine and provide readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–O. The complete documents support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original AgentRefine benchmark results, ablations, robustness experiments, human assessment of generated trajectories, and supplementary evaluations in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including the main benchmark comparisons and appendix experiments on filtering, Reflexion, robustness, and instruction following.

M1.justification: Script generation, trajectory generation, verification, and refinement tuning remain unchanged, including Equation (1) and Appendix O's algorithm. Figure 4 newly illustrates data conversion and error-token loss masking already described in v1.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same synthetic-data construction, ShareGPT experiments, five AgentBoard tasks, HotpotQA, and MT-bench. The evaluated perturbation scenarios and other task coverage also match.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain the same GPT-4o models, Llama/Mistral instruction models, AgentGen, AgentGym, and Agent-FLAN. Comparator membership in the appendix experiments is also unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendices A, D, and K retain the same evaluation sample sizes, model configurations, metrics, turn limits, training budgets, and perturbation procedures. No added experiment introduces a new protocol.

E4.justification: The refinement and masking ablations, data-scaling study, diversity analyses, perturbation tests, case studies, and judgment-reliability analysis are retained. Appendix filtering, Reflexion, component-robustness, and error-turn analyses also remain unchanged.

E5.justification: The ten evaluation samples at decoding temperature 1.0 and mean/standard-deviation reporting in Appendix H and Table 10 already appear in v1. v2 retains these practices and the same reporting of variability across perturbations.

E6.justification: Main and appendix result entries match. For example, Llama-3-8B AgentRefine's SciWorld success remains 14.4 in Table 1, and HotpotQA EM/F1 remains 37.0/44.6 in Figure 8. The plotted trends and qualitative cases are also unchanged.

T1.justification: The refinement-tuning objective and correctness indicator in Equation (1), and Appendix A's held-out aggregation formula, are unchanged. Neither version introduces additional formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about improved held-out generalization, perturbation robustness, thought diversity, and the connection between self-refinement and agent generalization.

C2.justification: Both retain the same memorization-versus-refinement explanation, interpretations of diversity and synthesis-model quality, and qualification about performance against held-in training methods. The ethics discussion and appendix interpretations are preserved despite relocation.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project-page link in the first-page footnote. Existing generation settings, training hyperparameters, and script, trajectory, and verification specifications remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive positioning against prior agent-tuning, synthetic-data, and self-refinement research are unchanged. The added acknowledgments do not alter research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 changes the header from 'Under review' to 'Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2025' and adds an acknowledgments section. There are limited emphasis and placement adjustments; the main prose and section sequence remain essentially unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 4 is expanded from data generation to the full pipeline, adding data conversion and loss-masking panels and revising its caption. v2 also adds a title icon and adjusts text and appendix layout. Other figures and tables retain their content.

improvement.justification: The expanded Figure 4 makes the connection between data construction and refinement training clearer, while the new project-page link provides an additional access pointer. These are modest improvements in exposition and accessibility; the method, empirical evidence, and scientific conclusions remain unchanged.
